sentences.text: In a two-year trial across eleven municipal offices, moving staff to a four-day week at full pay did not reduce the number of cases processed, lowered sick leave by a fifth and improved retention, but it lengthened waiting times for in-person services by about a day.
sentences.subject: A four-day week in municipal offices: results of a two-year trial

sentences.text: We describe the design, the outcomes and the limits of what the trial can show. ## Background
sentences.subject: A four-day week in municipal offices: results of a two-year trial

sentences.text: Interest in shorter working weeks has grown since several private firms reported gains in productivity and wellbeing.
sentences.subject: Background

sentences.text: Evidence from public administration is thinner, because public offices cannot easily shift demand and must remain open to citizens for fixed hours.
sentences.subject: Background

sentences.text: This trial asked whether a four-day week could be introduced in municipal offices without lowering the service citizens receive. ## Methods
sentences.subject: Background

sentences.text: Eleven offices were randomly assigned to the four-day schedule, and fourteen comparable offices kept the five-day week as controls.
sentences.subject: trial design

sentences.text: Offices were stratified by size and by the share of work that is done at a counter.
sentences.subject: trial design

sentences.text: Staff on the four-day schedule worked 32 hours across four days with no change in pay, and each office chose which weekday to close.
sentences.subject: trial design

sentences.text: The primary outcomes were the number of cases closed per employee per month, the days of sick leave, and the average waiting time for in-person services.
sentences.subject: outcomes

sentences.text: Secondary outcomes included staff turnover, a survey of citizen satisfaction and a validated measure of burnout.
sentences.subject: outcomes

sentences.text: Data were collected monthly for twenty-four months and analysed by an independent team that did not take part in the design.
sentences.subject: trial design

sentences.text: Cases closed per employee per month did not differ between the groups, with a mean of 61.2 in the four-day offices and 60.4 in the controls.
sentences.subject: cases closed

sentences.text: Sick leave fell by 21 percent in the four-day offices relative to controls, with the largest reductions among staff over fifty.
sentences.subject: sick leave

sentences.text: Turnover fell from 11.8 percent to 7.1 percent a year in the four-day offices, while the controls were unchanged.
sentences.subject: turnover

sentences.text: Waiting times for in-person services rose by an average of 0.9 days in the four-day offices, mainly in offices that closed on a Friday.
sentences.subject: waiting times

sentences.text: Citizen satisfaction scores were slightly lower in the four-day offices in the first six months and equal to the controls afterwards.
sentences.subject: citizen satisfaction

sentences.text: Burnout scores improved by 0.4 standard deviations among staff on the four-day schedule.
sentences.subject: burnout

sentences.text: The effect on sick leave was stable across all eleven offices and did not depend on which day they closed. ## Limitations
sentences.subject: sick leave

sentences.text: Offices knew which schedule they had, so neither staff nor managers were blind to the intervention, and some of the improvement in self-reported burnout may reflect expectation.
sentences.subject: Limitations

sentences.text: Eleven offices is a small sample, and the confidence intervals for turnover are wide.
sentences.subject: Limitations

sentences.text: The trial ran in a single country, with a particular labour law and a particular culture of public service.
sentences.subject: Limitations

sentences.text: We did not measure the quality of decisions, only their number and speed.
sentences.subject: Limitations

sentences.text: The trial suggests that a four-day week can be introduced in municipal offices without losing output, with real gains in health and retention, but at a cost in access for people who need a counter.
sentences.subject: Discussion

sentences.text: The waiting-time result is the one that matters most for policy, because it falls on citizens and not on staff.
sentences.subject: waiting times

sentences.text: Offices that kept a rotating rota so the counter stayed open five days saw almost none of the increase, which points to a design fix rather than a fundamental limit.
sentences.subject: rotating rota

sentences.text: Whether the gains would hold beyond two years is unknown.
sentences.subject: Limitations
